question: What will be the Port of Los Angeles's total container volume during October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Port guidance (Seroka, Oct 2026 briefing) is ~900k TEUs for October after a record 1,042,652 in September; 2026 Jun-Aug ran 956k-1,003k. Port Optimizer weekly import data shows October weeks up 27% (wk41) and ~65% (wk43 projected) YoY vs Oct 2025 (total 848k), suggesting upside to guidance; NRF expected October easing. Median slightly above guidance at ~922k. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; no Kalshi/bookmaker contract seen). Upper escape >1M priced ~8% given Q3 run-rate.

calls.reasoning: September 2026 set an all-time monthly record of 1,042,652 TEU. Seroka guided October to about 900k, but his September guidance undershot by about 140k. Port Optimizer weekly imports for October (about 105k, 133k and 118k TEU) run +13–27% YoY, which implies near-September import levels and roughly 950k–1.0M total. The NRF tracker expects October imports to ease and the season is a step down from the peak. Median 935k, with about 10% on exceeding 1M. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) late-October weekly import figures. Run 1 says Oct 25-31 is projected at +65% YoY; Run 3 says Oct 18-24 is 117.7k (+12.7%). Could not be settled without web access; the agreed-on Oct 11-17 figure (~133k, +19-27% YoY) plus Run 3's figures imply roughly 520-560k loaded imports. (2) Reliability of Seroka's ~900k guidance. Run 3's claim that the September guidance undershot by ~140k is unverified but plausible, so I treat the guidance as conservative. (3) Seasonal Oct/Sep ratio vs NRF easing is a judgment call. I take a median of 935k, above the guidance and below the pure weekly-data extrapolation, with a 10% upper escape because the weekly data points near 1M. Dispersion is in line with the runs.
